cases.given: a healthy workspace with no .deleting marker under any of its metadata IDs
cases.expected: the dialog renders identically to today — no cleanup section at all; absence of the section is the no-pending-cleanup signal

cases.given: a workspace whose store record has a .deleting marker and whose worktree root still exists on disk (a delete that failed before removal)
cases.expected: a cleanup section renders 'interrupted — worktree still present; workspace remains usable' with a pointer to warn-level delete logs; no finish/clear/retry call is issued

cases.given: a workspace surfaced by finishInterruptedDelete: marker exists, root is gone, the branch or metadata cleanup is outstanding
cases.expected: a cleanup section renders 'pending — worktree already removed, retry automatic on next load' plus the log pointer; the dialog performs no mutation

cases.given: a workspace whose legacy alias metadata ID carries the .deleting marker while the canonical MetadataID does not
cases.expected: the cleanup section still renders — the probe checks every ID in WorkspaceMetadataIDs(ws), mirroring finishInterruptedDelete

cases.given: a stored workspace record whose root was deleted out-of-band with no tombstone
cases.expected: no cleanup section renders (no tombstone means no amux-tracked pending cleanup); the plain path field still shows the absent root honestly as its stored value

cases.given: the cleanup probe (marker stat / root stat) cannot distinguish absence from error by signature
cases.action: open the status dialog on a workspace with missing identity fields or an unreadable store
cases.expected: the cleanup section renders 'unknown — could not read recovery state' rather than guessing pending/clean; the rest of the snapshot still renders

cases.given: a status open is in flight when the user opens a different dialog (bumping runOutputToken) or closes and reopens status
cases.action: deliver the workspaceStatusReadyMsg carrying cleanup probe results after the token advanced
cases.expected: the stale result is dropped — no dialog opens and no state mutates; identical fencing to the existing port/run reads

cases.given: the workspace is deleted or replaced after the status open captured ws.Clone() but before the result arrives
cases.action: the off-loop probe returns for the cloned snapshot
cases.expected: the rendered cleanup section describes the workspace as captured at open; the token fence still applies; no mutation touches the live workspace

cases.given: a tombstoned workspace whose root is gone but whose branch deletion keeps failing (non-not-found error) — the surfaced-row case
cases.expected: cleanup section shows pending-with-root-gone text; the surfaced workspace row remains visible; the section does not claim the branch specifically failed (that stage is not recorded)

cases.given: a tombstoned workspace suppressed from the list because session-kill or metadata-delete failed — invisible between loads
cases.action: open the status dialog if the row is reachable, else observe that the row is absent
cases.expected: if reachable, the pending text renders; if the row is suppressed by finishInterruptedDelete returning true, there is no status surface — the log is the record (documented limitation)

cases.given: a tombstoned workspace whose root has reappeared or was recreated between the marker write and now
cases.action: any diagnostic or hypothetical retry path evaluates the workspace
cases.expected: no destructive action is ever permitted against a live root — DirExists(root) aborts before any removal step, matching finishInterruptedDelete's pin; v1 exposes no retry action at all

cases.given: a workspace whose stamped alias set and recomputed identity differ (legacy vs canonical metadata ID)
cases.action: the cleanup probe runs over the workspace
cases.expected: the probe uses the same WorkspaceMetadataIDs alias set as the recovery path, so a tombstone under either form is detected and no identity assumption is fabricated

cases.given: a workspace with repo/project/workspace custom env vars whose values may hold secrets, plus a pending cleanup state
cases.expected: env rendering remains key-names-only and the cleanup section adds no new data fields derived from env or script content

cases.given: a tombstoned workspace with pending cleanup and a user who wants to force the retry now
cases.action: the user presses keys inside the status dialog
cases.expected: the dialog remains strictly read-only — every key keeps its existing OutputDialog meaning; no retry/force-delete affordance exists in v1
